## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the documentation and measured benchmark evidence updated to describe the consolidated read, so the next engineer can see what changed, why, the measured CPU reduction against the F10 baseline, and how to reproduce it.

## Scope

Parent AC3 (measurement evidence) and AC7 (documentation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` § "Cold-refresh cost" describes the consolidated read: one `wl worklist --json` per default-view tick, one read-cache entry, review-queue/browse derivation, the fail-open fallback, and that filtered views are unchanged.
- `CLI.md` documents `wl worklist` — purpose, options (`-n/--number`, `--prefix`), JSON payload shape (five subsets + metadata), pure-read/cacheable guarantee, and a usage example.
- Inline doc comments in `src/commands/worklist.ts`, `src/read-cache-cli.ts` (`READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` comment) and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` reflect the new path, cross-referencing the same rationale as the docs.
- The measured spawn count per default-view refresh is recorded in the doc (expected 5 → 1) and produced by the harness, not hand-waved.
- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts --query-set consolidated --json --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5` is executed and its CPU-seconds-per-cycle result is recorded on this work item and in the doc, compared against the pre-F4 baseline (159.44 CPU-s) and the F10 target (≤ 63.78 CPU-s).
- `npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts --json` spawn count and latency for a single default-view refresh are recorded on this work item.
- If the measured result misses the ≤ 0.4× target, the shortfall is documented with the measured number and an explicit follow-up note (no unsupported claims).
- Documentation mentions the backwards-compatibility fallback (older `wl` without the command) and the cross-subset consistency approach (one connection) including its residual risk.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC3: measured with `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10), total CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle with 4 panes drops to ≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline (≤ 63.8 CPU-s), ideally ~5× fewer spawns; this slice records the measured evidence.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC7: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (notably `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`).
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC8: the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Update `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` § 3 (Cold-refresh cost) with the consolidated-read bullet, revised spawn count and the new measured numbers.
2. Add the `wl worklist` entry to `CLI.md` (command reference + payload contract).
3. Update the header comments of the touched source modules.
4. Run both benchmarks with the consolidated query set, capture the JSON output, and paste the summary numbers into this work item as a comment plus the doc.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — cold-refresh cost section
- `CLI.md` — command reference for `wl worklist`
- `src/commands/worklist.ts`, `src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — doc comments
- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts`, `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` — measurement source (from WL-C1)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — refresh-cost note if it references spawn counts

## Dependencies

- Depends on WL-C5 (the wired refresh must exist before it can be measured).

## Deliverables

- Updated dev doc and CLI reference.
- Recorded benchmark evidence (CPU-seconds/cycle, spawn count, latency) with the comparison table.
- Comment on this item carrying the raw benchmark summary.

## Notes

- Follow the background-job etiquette for the benchmark runs (launch → prepare docs → one completion-aware wait → collect); do not poll with fixed `sleep`.
- Measurement must use the pre-compiled CLI (`dist/cli.js` or the bundled snapshot), not `tsx src/cli.ts` per spawn, or the numbers will not be comparable to F10's.

## Final re-audit attempt after the runner fix (2026-10-21 21:05 → 23:04)

**Runner fix is live.** SA-0MVI35BIU002MTZQ landed on SorraAgents dev (880db0477) and now also includes my corrected F3a/F3b findings: assessed exempt children no longer contribute blocking AC verdicts, the report names the real blocker with fallback provenance, and child-audit persistence is lifecycle-neutral (verified restore + dependent un-blocking). The main SorraAgents checkout was diverged (another agent's unpushed commit), so I integrated origin/dev by merge; the installed skill (symlink) now reports: restore helper present, F3a guard present, F3b branch present.

**Re-audit aborted on infrastructure, not on a verdict.** Ran `audit_runner.py issue WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B --force --no-child-in-main-slot` (9191 s):
- Phase 1 parent screening **129 s** (vs 763 s and a 1800 s timeout on earlier runs — the new concurrency ceiling helps).
- Phase 1 child screenings + Phase 2 parent deep completed.
- Aborted at child-audit persistence: `wl audit-set` could not acquire the worklog file lock (held 55 s by another process); the runner correctly fails closed rather than emit a parent report without child audits.
- Reliability: `calls=22 parse_ok=11 parse_failed=11 timeouts=9` — half the calls still wasted, mostly 600 s child-screen caps (SA-0MVI3608M0080QLW).

**No damage — and the fix is demonstrated.** Parent left `completed`/`in_review` (assignee cleared, `needsProducerReview: true`); **all 11 children remain `completed`/`in_review`** — zero demotions, zero `blocked`, which is exactly what previously broke. The stored parent verdict is still the old `Ready to close: No` (auditedAt 2026-10-21T11:58:59Z); nothing was overwritten by the aborted run.

**Resume state:** `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B.checkpoint.json` retains `phase1_parent` and `phase1_children` as completed at HEAD e1cedba5, so a resume can skip both — but the runner's freshness gate short-circuits a non-`--force` run (content unchanged), and `--force` discards checkpoints, so today a clean verdict requires one more full run when the host is quiet.

**Recommendation:** run the final `--force` re-audit during a low-contention window (the abort was pure lock contention from concurrent agents). All six parent ACs were `met`/`adjusted` on the previous complete run, the children are intact and exempt, and both runner defects that produced the false `No` are fixed.

## Measured evidence (same host + build: node v22.22.1, rgardler-AI-Laptop)

### bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts (4 panes, 30 s cycle, 5 s tick, 20 seeded items)

| Query set | Spawns / refresh | Spawns / cycle | CPU-s / cycle | p95 spawn wall | p50 | peak RSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `legacy` (4× `wl list` subsets + `wl next`) | 5 | 120 | 75.68 | 1227 ms | 1012 ms | 67.9 MB |
| `consolidated` (`wl worklist --json`) | **1** | **24** | **11.89** | **568 ms** | 505 ms | 67.8 MB |
| pre-F4 baseline (recorded on F10) | 5 | 120 | 159.44 | — | — | — |
| F10 target (≤ 0.4× pre-F4) | — | — | ≤ 63.78 | — | — | — |

- Spawn count per refresh: **5 → 1** (80 % fewer), 120 → 24 per cycle — all measured spawns were `cache-hit` (one write-free read populates the shared cache entry every pane reuses).
- CPU per cycle: **0.157×** the same-host legacy cost, **0.075×** the pre-F4 baseline — well below the ≤ 0.4× / ≤ 63.78 CPU-s target.
- p95 per-spawn wall time roughly halved (1227 → 568 ms).

### bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts --json (1000 items, 20 expanded parents, 30 browse)

| Query set | Spawns / refresh | Cold | Warm | within 2 s target |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `legacy` | 5 | 1187.5 ms | 628.8 ms | yes |
| `consolidated` | **1** | **892.9 ms** | **444.9 ms** | yes |

### Reproduce

```sh
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh:json -- --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5 --query-set consolidated
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh:json -- --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5 --query-set legacy
npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts --json --query-set consolidated
```

Shortfall: none — the ≤ 0.4× target is met with margin. Residual note: the review-queue subset uses hierarchy ordering rather than `wl list --stage in_review`'s 6-bucket order (that sort needs per-item git fingerprints; the bundle computes `currentFingerprint` only for audited items, so the banner state and membership are identical while the within-subset order can differ).
